title: Fly connections with 1 to 4 synapses repeat on the other brain side and in a second fly far above matched-overlap baselines, and a whole-brain spiking model needs their specific targets
abstract: Question: are fly connections below the common 5-synapse threshold reproducible wiring, and does a whole-brain model need them? In the FlyWire v783 release table, 1-4 synapse neuron pairs are 82% of connected pairs and 37% of synapses. Approach: we used cell types with one neuron per brain side (4,441 in FlyWire, 4,230 in the male CNS v1.0). For each connection we asked if the mirror connection is present on the other side, and in the other fly, and compared this with unconnected pairs that have the same expected contact opportunity (neuropil overlap in FlyWire, neuron totals in the male CNS). Results: a FlyWire 1-synapse connection was present on the other side in 31.2% of pairs against a 5.0% matched baseline; 2, 3 and 4 synapses gave 51%, 64% and 73%. The male CNS (FIB-SEM, other detector) gave 31.6% against 1.3%. Between flies, 37.7% of FlyWire 1-synapse connections were present in the male CNS (baseline 1.7%). An identical-wiring Poisson model limits reproduction of a 1-synapse connection to about 0.39-0.45; the observed values are 70-79% of this ceiling. 1-synapse connections found by only one of two FlyWire detectors still repeated in 18.5% of pairs (baseline 4.7%). In the Shiu et al. 2024 leaky integrate-and-fire model (10 sensory inputs per side, 19 sparse responses), removal of 1-4 synapse connections gave a median Jaccard overlap of active neurons of 0.72 with the full model against 0.94 between trial halves (p = 8e-6) and kept 76% of active neurons. A shuffle of weak-connection targets that keeps each neuron's weak input and output totals gave the same loss (0.71-0.73), so the model uses the specific weak routes. Random loss of the same synapse total gave 0.35. Results repeated at 150 Hz input. The sugar-to-MN9 prediction survived removal (62 vs 60 spikes/s). Limitations: neurons of singleton types are 6% of FlyWire neurons; baselines use neuropil-level or neuron-total overlap, not fine arbor contact; repeated systematic detection errors are not fully excluded; model results are for one LIF model with 10 trials and 10 sensory types. Conclusion: most 1-4 synapse connections are stereotyped wiring whose non-reproduction is mostly sampling, and a 5-synapse threshold removes specific routes that change whole-brain model responses.
